<jats:p>The approach (Paradigm) presented hereafter was inspired by two basic
ideas: assuming the MIMO-RIS-NOMA communication channel as a dispersive
channel with fading and representing the later by means of Generalized
Kroneker Channel model (GKCM) applying the so-called “Orthogonalization
Approach” based on the utilization of the “universal” eigenbasis in
the form of Prolate  Spheroidal Wave Functions (PSWF). In other words,
the essence of the approach lies in representing the MIMO-RIS-NOMA
channel by means of the finite set of artificially created orthogonal
trajectories for wave propagation (PSWF eigenbasis) depending to the
Planar Antenna(PA) patterns at the Transmitting and Receiving terminals
of MIMO systems, being connected between themselves by the so-called
Coupling Matrix (CM) of the RIS. Certainly, the goal for RIS (by certain
choice of the elements of CM) is to provide the system for the decoding
of the NOMA users with the required values of SNR for each user to
guarantee its successful decoding processing. Theoretical analysis of
this paradigm is presented in the following material.</jats:p>
title: An Approach for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) design for MIMO-NOMA Transmission: theoretical study

items.abstract: <jats:p>The material is dedicated to various aspects of graphene metasurface implementation of the Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) in the framework of the incoherent paradigm for NOMA-RIS-MIMO transmission design. Digital coded model of the metasurface is considered in the framework of the general representation of the graphene metasurface as a planar antenna array (PA). The simplification of the PA in the form of the non-uniform ULA (n-ULA) array and uniform linear array (ULA) is explained as well. In this regard array orthogonalization was applied in the form of the universal Prolate Spheroidal Wave Functions (PSWF) eigenbasis and it was used for the formulation of the RIS controller algorithm.</jats:p>
title: The Graphene Application for the Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (Ris) for the Noma-Ris-Mimo System Design. Phenomenological View
